findings.observed: Every 'add <task>' invocation prints 'added: <task>' and exits 0, but the added task never appears in 'list'. Reproduced with 6 distinct adds (todo, buy-bread, 任务-中文-test, multi word task, case-test, retry-test). 'list' output stayed exactly '[ ] buy milk' / '[ ] walk dog' throughout. No product-created state file appeared anywhere (project dir and user profile scanned). User input is silently lost.
findings.expected_basis: Discover packet purpose: 'A user can list tasks and add one with the Tasks CLI'. README describes a task list. The product's own 'added: X' confirmation asserts the add succeeded, contradicting the observed state.
findings.reproduction: 1) cd project dir; 2) python app/app.py add todo  -> 'added: todo', exit 0 (evidence runs/02); 3) python app/app.py list -> 'todo' absent (runs/03); 4) repeat with distinct names incl. unicode (runs/04, runs/13, runs/17); 5) filesystem scan shows no created state file (runs/06)

findings.observed: On a delivered state with no data file present, first 'list' prints '[ ] buy milk' and '[ ] walk dog' - two tasks no user added. The README documents no way to remove or complete tasks, and list output never changes regardless of usage (6/6 invocations identical).
findings.expected_basis: Fresh-state filesystem evidence (runs/00, runs/06) contradicts the listed content; README promises a 'Simple task list' of user tasks; a list the user cannot influence defeats the documented surface.
findings.reproduction: 1) verify app/ contains only app.py and README.md (evidence 00-app-dir-before.txt); 2) python app/app.py list -> two phantom tasks, exit 0 (runs/01); 3) run list after any adds -> identical output (runs/17)
findings.note: Distinct user-visible symptom from F-001 (phantom fixed content vs lost input); likely same root cause, to be linked at repair.

findings.observed: 'python app/app.py --help' and '-h' produce zero bytes on stdout and zero bytes on stderr and exit with code 2. In contrast, no-args and unknown commands print 'use: list | add <task>' with exit 0. A user following the universal help convention hits a silent dead end.
findings.expected_basis: The product's own feedback elsewhere (usage line on empty args) shows help text is the intended affordance; universal CLI convention is that --help/-h display usage.
findings.reproduction: 1) python app/app.py --help -> empty stdout, empty stderr, exit 2 (runs/08, captured on separate channels, run twice); 2) python app/app.py -h -> same (runs/09); 3) compare with python app/app.py frobnicate -> usage line (runs/10)

findings.observed: 'python app/app.py add' (no argument) and 'add ""' (empty string) both print 'added: None' and exit 0, leaking an internal placeholder token as a task-name confirmation and accepting invalid input without a validation error.
findings.expected_basis: The product's own confirmation format implies echoing a user-supplied task name; 'None' is not user input. Upstream taxonomy: form validation that accepts invalid input.
findings.reproduction: 1) python app/app.py add -> 'added: None', exit 0 (runs/11); 2) python app/app.py add "" -> 'added: None', exit 0 (runs/12)

findings.observed: Subcommands are case-sensitive: 'ADD retry-test' and 'List' fall through to the usage line 'use: list | add <task>' (exit 0), verified on two independent attempts. Exit-code conventions are also inconsistent: usage fall-through exits 0 while --help/-h exit 2.
findings.expected_basis: Common CLI convention treats commands case-insensitively or at least documents the constraint; the product's own exit codes are internally inconsistent (0 for invalid commands, 2 for help flags).
findings.reproduction: 1) python app/app.py ADD case-test -> usage line (runs/16); 2) retry python app/app.py ADD retry-test and python app/app.py List -> usage line both times (runs/18); 3) compare exit codes in runs/07, runs/08, runs/10
